entries.name: NASA Skywatching
entries.description: Read monthly skywatching guides, watch short videos, and learn observing basics for the Moon, planets, meteors, and eclipses. Check local visibility before using event suggestions.
entries.evidenceNote: Existing resource reverified by live open. Page has current October 2026 What’s Up guide, monthly video series, meteor shower articles, tips, and FAQ. No localized visibility guarantee.

entries.name: Stellarium
entries.description: Explore a realistic simulated sky, identify constellations and planets, and move through time before observing. Free desktop software includes telescope-oriented features; the official site also links to Stellarium Web.
entries.evidenceNote: Official homepage opened directly. Explicitly describes free open-source desktop software, time controls, telescope control, ocular simulation, and links to Stellarium Web. Free label describes this desktop resource, not all separately offered mobile products.

entries.name: timeanddate Astronomy
entries.description: Check local Sun and Moon times, Moon phases, planet visibility, and eclipse circumstances. Its location-based night-sky map and event explainers help turn a general sky event into a personal observing window.
entries.evidenceNote: Official astronomy hub and night-sky help page opened directly. Hub lists Sun/Moon calculators, eclipse lookup, meteor tools and night sky lookup. Help verifies location/date selection and object tracking. Map predictions do not confirm a user's unobstructed horizon or guarantee visibility.

entries.name: Photograph the Moon with a Smartphone
entries.description: Try Moon photography with practical advice on phone exposure, stability, zoom and editing. The guide explains digital-zoom limitations and automatic image enhancements that can affect the recorded detail.
entries.evidenceNote: Original official article credits Royal Observatory astronomer/astrophotographer Les Brand. Verified exposure, tripod/shutter-delay, optical-versus-digital-zoom, editing and smartphone AI-enhancement sections. No smartphone performance guarantee or inferred cost label.

entries.name: PhotoPills Academy
entries.description: Explore illustrated guides and videos for Milky Way, Moon, star trails and twilight photography. Some lessons teach PhotoPills workflows, so practical exercises can depend on its mobile app.
entries.evidenceNote: Opened official Academy listing and its Milky Way video lesson. Confirmed topic coverage and planning, equipment and camera-setting sections; omitted a cost label because the entire Academy's cost was not explicitly established.

entries.name: Astronomy 2e
entries.description: Read or download a complete introductory astronomy textbook covering the Solar System, stars, galaxies, and cosmology. Digital reading is free; printed editions and some supplementary products cost extra.
entries.evidenceNote: Live preface verified. Explicitly free web/PDF access and low-cost print; designed for one- or two-semester non-science-major courses. Avoid describing all OpenStax ancillary products as free.

entries.name: Clear Outside
entries.description: Choose a location to compare seven-day hourly cloud layers, weather, Moon times, and astronomical darkness. The traffic-light display makes a quick first check; revisit the forecast before heading out.
entries.evidenceNote: Official site opened and redirected to its default UK forecast. Page provides place/coordinate search, seven-day hourly forecasts, cloud layers, fog, Moon and darkness times, and explicitly free iOS/Android apps. Footer identifies First Light Optics. International title observed; no claim of exact global model coverage made.

entries.name: International Dark Sky Places
entries.description: Explore certified dark sky communities, parks, and protected areas around the world, and learn what certification protects. Confirm each destination’s opening hours, entry rules, and observing access separately.
entries.evidenceNote: Existing resource reverified by live open. Official program explains certification, worldwide coverage, and links to its searchable All Places directory. Certification does not establish unrestricted nighttime access.

entries.name: Cloudy Nights
entries.description: Discuss telescopes, binoculars, mounts and imaging with other observers. Use the dedicated imaging forums for astrophotography questions; the general beginners forum explicitly focuses on visual observing.
entries.evidenceNote: Official forum directory opened successfully, with equipment categories and the explicit Beginners Forum (No Astrophotography) restriction. Imaging category also opened; individual participant advice was not treated as verified technical guidance.

entries.name: PhotoPills
entries.description: Plan Milky Way, Moon and star-trail compositions with a mobile app, augmented reality views and exposure calculators. Available for iOS and Android; purchasing the app is required.
entries.evidenceNote: Official homepage confirms photography planning, Sun/Moon/Milky Way AR, exposure and star-trail tools, App Store/Google Play links and a purchase price. Exact price deliberately omitted.

entries.name: Galaxy Zoo
entries.description: Classify galaxy shapes in telescope images and discuss interesting objects with researchers and volunteers. Tutorials support beginners; available image collections change as research workflows progress.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official project page verified with Get Started/Classify and current Rubin workflow. Describes shape classification, learn-as-you-go process, and Talk community. No classifications submitted. Rendered count placeholders are zeros, so do not publish those counts.

entries.name: Light Pollution Map
entries.description: Compare satellite night-light layers, modeled sky brightness, and ground measurements while scouting darker areas. Check each layer's date and meaning; mapped darkness does not confirm public access or conditions tonight.
entries.evidenceNote: Official map and help opened directly. Help documents VIIRS night-light data, modeled sky-brightness/World Atlas layers, SQM measurements, sources and model caveats. It explicitly says modeled zenith brightness is a best-case estimate and not completely accurate everywhere. Access permissions and site safety are outside these data.

entries.name: Astrospheric
entries.description: Compare clouds, transparency, seeing, and smoke when planning North American observing. Forecast coverage follows regional weather models; check availability for your location. Free forecasts have partial data, with additional Pro features.
entries.evidenceNote: Homepage and official Data Domain documentation opened directly. RDPS coverage is regional rather than worldwide; ensemble component coverage is narrower. Documentation recommends checking Forecast Details availability. Homepage explicitly offers partial free forecast and paid Professional features. Forecast values are predictions, not observing guarantees.

entries.name: SkySafari
entries.description: Plan targets with interactive sky charts, observing lists, and an events calendar on iOS or Android. Paid editions offer different capabilities; check the edition and device requirements before choosing telescope-control features.
entries.evidenceNote: Official homepage, Pro product page, and official release landing page opened directly. Homepage lists paid Basic/Plus/Pro editions, observing tools and calendar; official landing page identifies Simulation Curriculum and mobile platforms. Avoid treating Pro capabilities as included in every edition.

entries.name: Sky Tonight
entries.description: Identify objects with a mobile sky map, follow their paths, and browse upcoming celestial events. The free app includes ads and limits expanded lists; paid access removes those restrictions.
entries.evidenceNote: Official product and support pages opened directly. Product lists tracking, AR, calendar and manually searchable objects. Support explicitly explains ads and blurred list entries beyond the first three until Premium or Lifetime access. Marketing stargazing index is not described here as a guarantee.

entries.name: Stargazing Basics
entries.description: Build practical observing skills with the magazine's beginner collection: learning constellations, reading star charts, and starting with a telescope. Choose a guide for your next step rather than tackling everything at once.
entries.evidenceNote: Publisher's own collection opened directly. Introduction and article links explicitly cover unaided-eye observing, constellations, star wheels/charts and first telescope setup. Mixed publication dates mean this evergreen collection should not be represented as a current event calendar.

entries.name: meteoblue Astronomy Seeing
entries.description: Compare worldwide cloud layers, atmospheric seeing, and jet-stream forecasts before telescope sessions. Three days are free; seven days require point+. Fog and very low clouds need a separate check.
entries.evidenceNote: Generic official seeing route opened successfully and selected a default location; users must set their own. It explicitly lists three-day and subscribed seven-day access and missing fog/very low clouds. English help fetch returned an internal error; official German help loaded and verifies worldwide coverage, independent seeing/cloud indices and forecast limitations. No live forecast values are reproduced.

entries.name: Clear Sky Chart
entries.description: Read compact hourly charts for clouds, transparency, seeing, and darkness at observing sites in Canada, the United States, and parts of Mexico. Select a nearby chart and check its forecast timestamp.
entries.evidenceNote: Official homepage and linked example/chart explanation opened directly. Homepage explicitly gives Canada/USA/parts of Mexico coverage, hourly variables and no-cost chart requests with optional sponsorship. Site says maintained by CSCCharts after Attilla Danko's death. Do not infer a chart's existence grants site access.

entries.name: NOAA Aurora Forecast
entries.description: Check modeled aurora location and intensity for both hemispheres over the next 30–90 minutes. This short-term outlook still depends on darkness, local weather, and available solar-wind observations.
entries.evidenceNote: Original official SWPC URL opened and redirected to spaceweather.gov. NOAA page explains OVATION's 30–90-minute lead, both hemisphere maps and fallback without lead time when input data are missing/contaminated. Linked official viewing tips opened. Page returned stale-looking time/no-data widgets, so no claim is made about current activity or operational freshness.

entries.name: Meteor Shower FAQ
entries.description: Prepare for a meteor watch with advice on timing, direction, dark adaptation, and comfortable setup. Learn why radiant height, moonlight, and local conditions make published meteor rates different from what you see.
entries.evidenceNote: Legacy meteor FAQ URL now links to the current /faq/ page, which opened directly. It explains unaided-eye observing, radiant/location limits, moonlight, adaptation, setup and the distinction between ZHR and actual observed rate. Use current /faq/ destination.

entries.name: Eclipse Viewing Safety
entries.description: Understand eye protection for partial, annular, and total solar eclipses, including indirect viewing. NASA explains why eclipse glasses cannot replace the special front-mounted solar filters required for binoculars or telescopes.
entries.evidenceNote: Current NASA safety guide opened directly. It distinguishes partial/annular viewing from the brief total phase, requires specialized solar eye protection, describes indirect projection, warns against using eclipse glasses through optics, and requires special-purpose front filters for optics with expert advice. NASA does not approve viewer brands.

entries.name: Heavens-Above
entries.description: Set your observing location to find ISS and bright-satellite passes, with times and sky charts. Check predictions close to your session; orbital forecasts become less accurate farther from the current date.
entries.evidenceNote: Official root opened successfully and lists location configuration, ISS/bright satellite predictions and sky charts, with optional login. Parameterized official FAQ opened and verifies local-time tables and declining accuracy farther from current time. Bare FAQ/main routes intermittently errored; root and parameterized FAQ succeeded. No claim that any listed pass will be visible through weather or local obstructions.

entries.name: Where to Stargaze
entries.description: Explore U.S. national parks with night-sky programs and ideas for observing closer to home. Follow each park's own pages for current events, opening hours, reservations, and overnight access before traveling.
entries.evidenceNote: Official NPS page opened directly; it includes home observing ideas, a partial list of parks offering night-sky programs, and links to park pages and event calendar. Page last-updated date is July 24, 2025. Directory inclusion is not current confirmation of nighttime access, event availability, reservations, fees or safety.

entries.name: Siril
entries.description: Calibrate, align, stack and process astronomical images with desktop software. Follow the official tutorials for a first workflow and for preparing the calibration frames your images need.
entries.evidenceNote: Official homepage confirms calibration, stacking, enhancement and desktop downloads; first-steps tutorial specifies biases/darks/flats/lights folders and RAW-only input for its workflow. Cost label omitted rather than inferred.

entries.name: N.I.N.A.
entries.description: Automate deep-sky imaging through equipment connections, focusing and sequencing, supported by official documentation and a quick start. Requires a compatible Windows computer and supported cameras, mounts or drivers.
entries.evidenceNote: Official introduction states automated DSO imaging and free/open-source distribution; requirements specify Windows 10 64-bit or later and enumerate native and ASCOM device support. Documentation warns screenshots may lag software updates.

entries.name: PHD2 Guiding Manual
entries.description: Learn guide-camera and mount connections, calibration, guiding graphs and troubleshooting from PHD2's manual. Intended for imaging setups with guiding equipment; device-specific connection requirements still apply.
entries.evidenceNote: Official project site identifies PHD2 as telescope guiding software and links this manual. Manual contains equipment connection, calibration, monitoring, polar alignment and troubleshooting sections; basic-use page documents guide camera/mount selection.

entries.name: Astrophotography 101
entries.description: Follow a free lesson collection covering Milky Way capture, lenses, focusing, stacking and processing. Several lessons reflect older equipment or software, and some listed topics remain unfinished.
entries.evidenceNote: Original creators' official lesson hub explicitly says the series is completely free and lists shooting, equipment, post-processing and advanced topics. Page shows its older update date and multiple Coming Soon entries; commercial affiliate disclosure is present.

entries.name: Stellafane Beginner Resources
entries.description: Build observing habits before choosing equipment, with beginner articles on learning the sky, binoculars and a first telescope. This is a starting guide with some older external references.
entries.evidenceNote: Official Springfield Telescope Makers beginner page and its original Steve Dodson article opened. Verified learn-the-sky, binocular, red-light and star-party advice. External directories/book recommendations not individually verified; historical prices intentionally excluded.

entries.name: ASTAP
entries.description: Stack deep-sky images, inspect FITS files and solve image coordinates with ASTAP. Its official page includes a detailed manual; plate solving requires installing an appropriate star database.
entries.evidenceNote: Author's official page explicitly describes a free stacking and astrometric solver, includes FITS viewing and documentation, and instructs installation of the program plus one star database. Current desktop platform installers listed; no universal device compatibility claim.

entries.name: AutoStakkert!
entries.description: Align and stack lunar and planetary image sequences using lucky-imaging software and its official guides. Windows software; additional sharpening is needed, and commercial use requires a purchased license.
entries.evidenceNote: Official features page verifies image-sequence alignment/stacking and explicitly excludes final sharpening/post-processing. Download page confirms Windows-only native software, freeware private use and free educational/charity use, with purchase required for business/commercial use.

entries.name: FireCapture
entries.description: Capture planetary video with camera profiles, automated recording and session logs, supported by installation and first-step tutorials. Check the official camera and operating-system compatibility table before installing.
entries.evidenceNote: Author's official website confirms planetary capture purpose, camera/OS compatibility matrix, capture profiles, autorun, logs and first-step tutorials. Did not infer licensing from a joking 'bugs—all free' banner; cost label deliberately omitted.

entries.name: StarStaX
entries.description: Blend a sequence of night photographs into star trails, with gap filling and an official tutorial. Available for Windows and macOS; develop RAW files elsewhere before importing.
entries.evidenceNote: Author's official page confirms star-trail blending, gap filling, Windows/macOS and lack of RAW development. Official license explicitly permits free use including commercial projects, while clarifying the software is not open source.

entries.name: Meteors and Meteorites
entries.description: Understand how meteoroids, meteors, and meteorites differ, explore their origins, and follow links to meteor science and observing information. This is background learning rather than a local forecast.
entries.evidenceNote: Existing resource reverified by live open. NASA explainer distinguishes the three terms and links to meteor showers and related facts.

entries.name: Five Principles for Responsible Outdoor Lighting
entries.description: Learn how to direct, control, and reduce outdoor lighting, with downloadable materials for explaining the principles to others. Translations include Bengali; local lighting requirements still need separate checking.
entries.evidenceNote: Live page verified; updated September 30, 2026. Five principles, PDF/PNG downloads, and Bengali plus other translations are listed. Page explicitly permits free download and unmodified distribution.

entries.name: Galaxies, Stars and Planets
entries.description: Follow an introductory course on cosmic scale, gravity, the Solar System, stars, and galaxies. Reading can start immediately; an account enables progress tracking, quizzes, and a participation statement.
entries.evidenceNote: Live course page verified. Explicitly free, introductory, eight hours; no signup needed to read, signup for tracking, full activities, and free Statement of Participation. Last content update listed as 2018.

entries.name: General Relativity Video Lectures
entries.description: Watch graduate lectures on tensors, spacetime curvature, gravitational waves, cosmology, and black holes, supported by course problem sets. This advanced course requires substantial mathematics and physics preparation.
entries.evidenceNote: Live video gallery verified. Twenty-three lecture titles, graduate level, and problem sets listed. OCW explicitly free and self-study, with no certificate or degree credit.

entries.name: astroEDU
entries.description: Find peer-reviewed astronomy activities for classrooms and outreach, with age ranges and practical teaching instructions. Review each activity’s materials, timing, and language before adapting it for your group.
entries.evidenceNote: Live library and About pages verified. Open-access activities reviewed by a scientist and educator; CC BY 4.0 license. OAE resources page separately confirms English, French, Greek, Italian, and Spanish editions.

entries.name: Astronomical Society of India Outreach
entries.description: Explore astronomy activities, public education resources, and outreach initiatives connected to India’s professional astronomy community. Many pages archive past campaigns, so verify dates before treating an announcement as current.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official hub and charter verified. Resources and activities cover multiple age groups; 2026 outreach alongside older campaign archives. Do not claim its amateur-group form is an established club finder or general society membership application.

entries.name: Getting Started with Variable Star Observing
entries.provider: American Association of Variable Star Observers
entries.description: Learn to observe variable stars and contribute measurements to scientific archives, with guidance on techniques, targets, and equipment. A free account supports data submission; some additional services require membership.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official Getting Started page verified. Free account provides forums, Special Interest Groups, and archive submissions; membership enables mentor requests and robotic network. Manuals include visual/digital photometry and spectroscopy. No price label inferred from membership wording.

entries.name: Planet Hunters TESS
entries.description: Help search TESS observations for signs of planets beyond the Solar System, using guided online classifications and discussions. Candidate signals need scientific follow-up before they can establish a planet discovery.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official project verified with Get Started, Classify, and Talk. Results page updated October 15, 2026. NASA directory confirms TESS data and smartphone/laptop participation. No classification submitted or discovery guarantee.

entries.name: The Daily Minor Planet
entries.description: Review Catalina Sky Survey image sequences to help distinguish possible asteroids from false detections. Follow the project’s instructions for contribution credit; reviewing a candidate does not guarantee a new discovery.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official project verified with active Get Started/Classify links, Catalina survey description, daily updated task, and separate form for measurer credit. No form completed, external message sent, or classification submitted.

entries.name: Astronomical League Observing Programs
entries.description: Build observing skills with structured target lists, log guidance, and programs for different objects and instruments. Read each program’s rules carefully, especially membership and award requirements.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official pages verified. Programs teach navigation, instruments, and observation recording. Awards have differing eligibility: Youth Silver explicitly permits nonmembers, Gold requires membership. Manuals may be sold through the store; omit global cost label.

entries.name: British Astronomical Association
entries.description: Join an international amateur astronomy community with observing sections, expert advice, publications, talks, and challenges for several experience levels. Membership is paid; many in-person activities take place in Britain.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official join page verified. Explicit subscription rates, worldwide members, digital/print options, section support, online talks, tutorials, and beginner/advanced challenges. No exact prices copied; no claim every member resource is publicly accessible.

entries.name: Home Outdoor Lighting Assessment
entries.description: Use a worksheet to assess outdoor lights at home, identify fixtures needing changes, and plan improvements using responsible lighting principles. The assessment is practical guidance rather than a professional audit.
entries.evidenceNote: Live page verified. Contains downloadable assessment worksheet, scoring/action instructions, and advice on shielding, brightness, controls, and color. No cost label inferred.

entries.name: Astronomy Education Resources
entries.provider: IAU Office of Astronomy for Education
entries.description: Browse multilingual astronomy teaching resources, a terminology glossary, education guides, and light pollution or eclipse collections. Language coverage differs between collections, so check the linked resource before planning lessons.
entries.evidenceNote: Live official resources page verified. Lists topical/document search, multilingual glossary, education reviews, light pollution awareness, eclipse resources, and language choices. No implication all materials have every translation.

entries.name: SIMBAD Astronomical Database
entries.description: Look up astronomical objects by name or coordinates, with identifiers, measurements and references to published research. Covers objects outside the Solar System; consult the original studies when interpreting data.
entries.evidenceNote: Parent independently opened the official CDS service. It explicitly provides name/coordinate queries, bibliography, measurements and cross-identifications for objects outside the Solar System; service is free without registration. No query results or object counts copied.

deferred.name: Astronomy & Astrophysics — An Introductory Survey
deferred.provider: IAU OAE Center India and ASI POEC
deferred.reason: Official search-index text verifies G. Srinivasan lecture series and video playlist covering radiation, relativity, stellar evolution, galaxies, compact objects, and cosmology. Direct opens repeatedly return 502; recheck before publication.

deferred.name: Backyard Worlds: Planet 9
deferred.reason: NASA participation guide is current, but official Zooniverse research page explicitly says Finished/out of data and new batch being prepared. Do not publish as immediately active; can be added later with availability note.

deferred.name: Globe at Night
deferred.reason: Official NOIRLab toolkit verifies global sky-brightness reporting function. Live main/www/instructions/webapp opens return 403 or fetch errors, and current site search yields no indexed results. No current campaign dates or functioning submission flow verified, so defer rather than declare active or offline.

deferred.name: Astrophysics Data System
deferred.reason: Official indexed About page verified; automated opens hit bot verification and parent browser rendered navigation/footer without the search panel. Deferred in favor of the directly verified SIMBAD service.

deferred.name: VizieR
deferred.reason: Official route returned an access-denied page during parent verification.

deferred.name: International Meteor Organization calendar
deferred.reason: Researcher found restoration pages at the calendar PDF destinations; omitted until working content can be checked.

deferred.name: Sequator
deferred.reason: Official site redirected to Google sign-in during researcher verification; omitted rather than using a mirror.

deferred.reason: Official reader-facing site timed out during researcher verification; omitted rather than using similarly named third-party sites.
